cells.tense: You are steering by your own light and the wheel is in your hands.
cells.ask: Back one direction you've already chosen with something visible — a block on the calendar, a first payment, a told someone. Hold it without defending it.
cells.core:
You know which way you're headed and you're not arguing about it. The direction came before the reasons did, and that's how you can tell it's yours — it landed without an argument.

You're pointed, and the pointing is quiet. You don't need anyone to agree with it for it to hold, and the light you're moving toward does the deciding, not the people watching. Keep that. The cost is that nobody hands you a map back — the direction stays yours to carry, day by day, with no applause. Support here isn't a rescue. It's strength arriving from somewhere outside you, spent on what you're already pointed at.
cells.sheetLine: Your direction landed before the reasons did.
cells.verb: choosing a direction from vision and holding to it
cells.place: becoming what you are — no dimming

cells.tense: You are aiming at a version of this that hasn't happened yet and can't be written in.
cells.ask: Name the next real step out loud to one witness, and let their plain questions land unanswered for the rest of the day.
cells.core:
You're living a few turns ahead of where you actually are. The calling has to arrive finalized, proven, beyond objection before you'll let it be current — so the present keeps getting audited for whether it's really it.

When this holds, you're pointed at one light and the way there is visible in steps, not in verdicts. What's bending now is that the direction has to be defended before it's walked, and every challenge gets met with more case. You don't know yet what it will become — nobody does at the start — and holding that unclosed is the work here. Discernment right now is the honest kind: noticing which pull you felt and which one you built an argument for. You can't perfect a direction into being real. So let a plain question land, and don't answer it.

cells.tense: You stopped saying which way you were headed, and the stopping has its own momentum now.
cells.ask: Say one direction out loud to a single person this week — badly is fine. Then stop and don't sell it.
cells.core:
There's a direction you haven't said out loud in a while. It's not gone — it's just unspoken, and saying it out loud stopped at some point. What would help isn't a new calling. It's pointing at the one you have.

When this holds, what you are shows up in the open and you enjoy it — things you tended reaching their finish, no dimming. Lately it runs low, so it stays private. Don't try to feel your way back into it; feeling pushed at something low doesn't land. Put energy into care instead, the kind that doesn't exhaust: water one thing you're already growing and let that tending be the practice. The growth is the point, not the proving. One direction, said plainly to one person, is the whole act.
cells.sheetLine: The direction is still yours. You just stopped saying it.
cells.verb: choosing a direction from vision and holding to it
cells.place: becoming what you are — no dimming

cells.tense: You are steering by a chosen direction and calling it just how things happened.
cells.ask: Write down the last three turns you decided — only the ones you actually made — and leave them somewhere you'll see them.
cells.core:
You've already chosen which light you're moving toward. It shapes your days — what you say yes to, what you let pass, where the time goes. But the story you tell has the direction arriving from outside, as if events pointed you rather than you pointing yourself.

The steering is happening. Saying so isn't, and saying so is the smaller, earlier step, easy to skip. When this holds, what you are shines out because the work came first; the shine follows, so there's something to stand on. What's absent isn't shine. It's taking the credit. Help here isn't advice — it's strength from somewhere outside you, used to hold what you've already decided. Name one turn as yours and let it stand.
cells.sheetLine: You made the call. You talk like events did.

The asks are doable either way and promise nothing, since each is an act with a finish and a day's horizon. The sentence that serves the writer is the one about the room behind them; it is cut, and the cell only says the saying stopped.
